In /bench/repo (the memos Go repo), investigate with thoroughness "very thorough" and report exact file paths and line numbers:

A) Identity provider (SSO) support: which package defines the provider abstraction/interface (likely internal/idp) and which concrete protocol implementation package ships (e.g. internal/idp/oauth2)? List files and the interface name, path:line. Is there an OIDC/SAML/LDAP impl too? List all subpackages of internal/idp.

B) MySQL driver construction: find where store/db/mysql.NewDB (or equivalent constructor, check store/db/mysql/*.go for its constructor name) is called. There should be a driver-selection factory (store/db/db.go NewDBDriver or similar). Run `grep -rn "mysql.NewDB\|NewDB(" --include=*.go` across the repo and report EVERY call site, including tests. State whether any non-factory production code constructs the MySQL driver directly. Cite the factory path:line and the grep evidence.

C) Default installation dispatch: with no database flags, which driver is default (check profile defaults, cmd/memos/main.go, internal/profile/profile.go — likely sqlite). Which concrete method executes the SQL INSERT when a memo is created — find CreateMemo in store/db/sqlite/memo.go (path:line) vs mysql and postgres versions, and explain the dispatch: store.Store holds a Driver interface, chosen in the factory based on profile.Driver default value. Cite: default driver value path:line, factory switch path:line, sqlite CreateMemo path:line.

D) Close methods: run `grep -rn "func (.*) Close(" --include=*.go` in the repo (exclude web/). Count distinct method declarations named Close across the backend Go code. Then find which ones are actually invoked by non-test server code (grep for `.Close()` callers in cmd/, server/, store/ non-test files) — e.g. store.Close, db driver Close, etc. Report count and invoked declarers with caller path:line.

Report facts with path:line citations, concise.

content.text:
## A) Identity provider (SSO) support

**Package layout — only two packages exist:**
- `/bench/repo/internal/idp/idp.go` (7 lines total)
- `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`, `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2_test.go`

**Subpackages of `internal/idp`: exactly one — `oauth2`.** No OIDC, SAML, or LDAP implementation exists anywhere (the only `oidc` hits in the repo are doc comments in generated protobuf files, e.g. `/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/auth_service_grpc.pb.go:35`; no `saml`/`ldap` hits at all).

**There is no provider interface.** `/bench/repo/internal/idp/idp.go:3` declares only a shared data struct `IdentityProviderUserInfo` (fields Identifier, DisplayName, Email, AvatarURL). That struct is the entire "abstraction" — there is no `type IdentityProvider interface`.

The concrete type is a struct, not an interface implementation:
- `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:20` — `type IdentityProvider struct` (holds `*storepb.OAuth2Config`)
- `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:27` — `NewIdentityProvider(config *storepb.OAuth2Config) (*IdentityProvider, error)`
- `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:47` — `ExchangeToken` (supports PKCE)
- `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:83` — `UserInfo` returns `*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo`

Sole consumer: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:121` calls `oauth2.NewIdentityProvider(identityProvider.Config.GetOauth2Config())` directly — no polymorphic dispatch.

The proto confirms single-protocol design: `/bench/repo/proto/store/idp.proto:11-14` — enum `Type` has only `TYPE_UNSPECIFIED = 0; OAUTH2 = 1;`, and `IdentityProviderConfig` (`:21-25`) is a oneof with a single member `oauth2_config`.

## B) MySQL driver construction

**Constructor name: `NewDB`** — `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20` → `func NewDB(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error)`.

**Factory: `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:14` — `NewDBDriver(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error)`**, switching on `profile.Driver` at `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:18`.

Full grep evidence (`grep -rn "mysql.NewDB\|NewDB(" --include=*.go`) — every hit in the repo:

| path:line | kind |
|---|---|
| `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:20` | factory call `sqlite.NewDB(profile)` |
| `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:22` | factory call `mysql.NewDB(profile)` — **only** MySQL construction site |
| `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:24` | factory call `postgres.NewDB(profile)` |
| `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:24` | declaration |
| `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/postgres.go:21` | declaration |
| `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20` | declaration |
| `/bench/repo/store/demo_seed_test.go:24` | **test** — `sqlite.NewDB(p)` direct |
| `/bench/repo/store/deployment_config_test.go:416` | **test** — `sqlite.NewDB(p)` direct |

**No non-factory production code constructs the MySQL driver directly.** The only two direct-constructor bypasses are test files, and both use sqlite, not mysql. `NewDBDriver` callers: `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go:57` (production), `/bench/repo/store/test/store.go:28` and `:50`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/memo_service_benchmark_test.go:70` (test harnesses).

## C) Default installation dispatch — sqlite

**Default driver value:** `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go:122` — `viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")`, reinforced by the flag default at `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go:130` (`rootCmd.PersistentFlags().String("driver", "sqlite", ...)`). Read into the profile at `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go:43`.

`/bench/repo/internal/profile/profile.go:30` declares `Driver string` (comment at `:29` says "sqlite, mysql" — stale, postgres is also supported). Profile has no hardcoded default itself; `Validate()` at `/bench/repo/internal/profile/profile.go:110` only derives the DSN when `p.Driver == "sqlite" && p.DSN == ""`, producing `<dataDir>/memos_prod.db` (`:115-116`).

**Factory switch:** `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:18-27`; the `"sqlite"` arm is `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:20`.
